content.summary: Reviewed asynchronous transport, immutable reports, local meaning authority, archive migration, exact candidate/report/source binding and the old release API before combined interpretation and legacy service acceptance.
findings: The API accepts an enumerated scripted adapter configuration, never arbitrary code or supplied reviewer authority. Source inventory and proposals are separate requests.

Meaning acceptance is derived from the identity registry and the exact source/candidate/report hashes. A ready report cannot grant release; existing build/applicability and two-role review remain required.
All associated runs are checked through Lifecycle approval, Releases release, current selection and Java export. One clean investigation cannot hide another unfinished bound run.
Authenticated source invalidation blocks current use while the immutable historical report still verifies. Explicit successor review is required to supersede an earlier investigation.
Archive export includes all interpretation projections and histories, while import remains compatible with prior archives and keeps login tokens disabled.
The UI displays source text using textContent, retains dissent and uncertainty, and requires exact report identities for review. Browser interaction and packaging remain P4 checks.
The comparison integration tests use the actual Java interpreter to replay SMT witnesses; they do not establish correspondence with the English circular.
